Exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis for each dimension

Source: R/GLM_VALIDITY.R
compute_efa_cfa.Rd

For every dimension of a questionnaire, fits three exploratory factor analysis (EFA) models with psych::fa and two one-factor confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) models with lavaan::cfa, and collects their loadings, fit indices, modification indices, residuals, factor scores and score correlations. All results are also written to an Excel workbook.

Usage

compute_efa_cfa(
  dimensions,
  df_response,
  filename = "efa_cfa_models.xlsx",
  mini = 1,
  maxi = 5
)

Arguments

dimensions

Data frame with one row per item and the columns dimension (the dimension the item belongs to), subquestion_text (the name of the item's column in df_response) and key (1 for an item that is reverse scored, -1 for an item scored as it is; see Details).

df_response

Data frame of numeric item responses with one column per item, named as in dimensions$subquestion_text. Missing responses must be NA; recode missing-data codes (such as 0) to NA first.

filename

Path of the Excel file to write. Its folder is created if it does not exist. Default "efa_cfa_models.xlsx" in the working directory.

mini, maxi

Lowest and highest possible response. They are used to reverse score items (mini + maxi - x). Defaults 1 and 5.

Value

A list with

efa_cfa_models

One row per item with n, dimension, variable and F1 (Model 1 loadings); S2F1, S2F2 (Model 2 structure matrix, the correlations of the items with the rotated factors); P2F1, P2F2 (Model 2 pattern matrix, the regression weights of the rotated factors); S3F1 to S3F3 and P3F1 to P3F3 (the same for Model 3); index with f1_v, f2_v, f3_v (EFA fit of Models 1 to 3: RMSEA with its lower and upper limits and confidence level, RMS, CFI, TLI); unstandardized and standardized (Model 4 loadings); unstandardized_RI, standardized_RI, RI_u and RI_s (Model 5 loadings and random intercept loadings); index_cfa with fit_CFA and fit_CFA_RI (CFA fit of Models 4 and 5: RMSEA with its limits, SRMR, CFI, TLI). A dimension with fewer than 7 items gets extra rows (without a variable) for the EFA fit indices.

cfa_scores

Factor scores of Model 4 (lavaan::lavPredict), one column per dimension whose CFA ran and one row per row of df_response (NA for respondents without any answer in that dimension).

plots_scree

An empty list (the scree plot code is switched off).

cfa_coefficients

Model 4 loadings (lambda), residual variances (theta) and intercepts, standardized and unstandardized, one row per item.

The Excel file has the sheets critical (efa_cfa_models, with loadings beyond 0.32 or below -0.32 highlighted), CFA_Modification_Indexes (Model 4 modification indices of 10 or more), EFA1F_Residuals (Model 1 residual correlations beyond 0.1 in absolute value), CFA_Coefficients, CFA_RI_Coefficients, used_items (correlations of the items with the dimension mean scores), used_items_item_correlation (item pairs sorted by the size of their correlation), used_items_mean_score and used_items_cfa_score (correlations between the dimension mean scores and between the CFA scores). A sheet without any content (for example when no CFA ran) is not written.

Details

The models fitted for each dimension are

  1. Model 1: one-factor EFA (maximum likelihood).

  2. Model 2: two-factor EFA (maximum likelihood, oblimin rotation).

  3. Model 3: three-factor EFA (maximum likelihood, oblimin rotation).

  4. Model 4: one-factor CFA (missing = "ML", with means).

  5. Model 5: Model 4 plus a random intercept factor RI, with all its loadings fixed to 1 and unrelated to the dimension's factor.

An EFA model that is not identified for the number of items (negative degrees of freedom), or that fails, is reported as NA: the one-factor model needs at least 3 items, the two-factor model 5 and the three-factor model 6. The CFA models need at least 4 items, because with 3 items the random intercept model has more parameters than the data can identify (lavaan fits it without a warning, so the function skips it).

The EFA and CFA models use the responses as they are, so items worded in the opposite direction have negative loadings. The mean scores and the correlation sheets use reverse scored items: psych::reverse.code is called with key * -1, so the items with key = 1 are reversed.

Warnings from lavaan (for example about respondents without any answer) are shown as messages and do not stop the CFA. If a CFA model stops with an error or does not converge, the CFA columns of that dimension are NA and the function continues with the next dimension. In the lavaan models, a dimension name that is not a syntactically valid R name (for example one with spaces) is changed with make.names.

The function stops with an error if dimensions lacks one of its columns, if key has values other than 1 and -1, or if an item is not a numeric column of df_response. It warns about responses outside mini to maxi and about items without variance (no responses, or the same response from everyone), because the EFA and CFA of their dimension fail.

The function needs the rwf functions model_loadings, c_bind, change_data_type, matrix_triangle, excel_critical_value and excel_matrix.

Note

Most of the run time is spent writing the Excel file, because excel_critical_value adds conditional formatting one cell at a time.

Examples

# \donttest{
items<-c(paste0("E",1:10),paste0("N",1:10),paste0("A",1:10),
         paste0("C",1:10),paste0("O",1:10))
reverse_items<-c("E2","E4","E6","E8","E10","N2","N4","A1","A3","A5",
                 "A7","C2","C4","C6","C8","O2","O4","O6")
df<-df_ocean[,items]
df[df==0]<-NA # 0 is the missing-data code of df_ocean
dimensions<-data.frame(dimension=substr(items,1,1),
                       subquestion_text=items,
                       key=ifelse(items%in%reverse_items,1,-1))
result<-compute_efa_cfa(dimensions=dimensions,
                        df_response=df[1:2000,],
                        filename=file.path(tempdir(),"efa_cfa_ocean.xlsx"))
#> Dimension: A
#> Dimension: C
#> Dimension: E
#> Dimension: N
#> Dimension: O
